source.text: וַיָּ֡קָם אֶלְיָשִׁיב֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְאֶחָ֣יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת־שַׁ֣עַר הַצֹּ֔אן הֵ֣מָּה קִדְּשׁ֔וּהוּ וַֽיַּעֲמִ֖ידוּ דַּלְתֹתָ֑יו וְעַד־מִגְדַּ֤ל הַמֵּאָה֙ קִדְּשׁ֔וּהוּ עַ֖ד מִגְדַּ֥ל חֲנַנְאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And arose Eliashib the priest, the great, and his brothers the priests, and they built the gate of the sheep; they consecrated it and set up its doors; and as far as [the] tower of the Hundred they consecrated it, as far as [the] tower of Hananel.

en.L: And Eliashib the high priest arose with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
en.B: Then Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests set to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They dedicated it and set its doors in place. They built and dedicated the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel.
en.R: Eliashib the high priest and the other priests started the work. They rebuilt the Sheep Gate, set its doors in place and dedicated it to God. They also rebuilt the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel, and dedicated it.

decisions.choice: Eliashib the high priest: the head of the priests in Nehemiah's time
decisions.reason: Eliashib was the grandson of Jeshua, the high priest of the first return (12:10; Ezra 3:2). The list of builders begins with the priests, at the part of the wall nearest the temple. Later Eliashib let Tobiah use a room in the temple (13:4-7).

decisions.choice: the Sheep Gate, the Tower of the Hundred, the Tower of Hananel: the northeast of the city, north of the temple
decisions.reason: The list goes around the wall counterclockwise, from the Sheep Gate in the northeast (compare John 5:2) west along the north wall, down the west side, and back up the east (3:1-32), ending again at the Sheep Gate (3:32). The Tower of Hananel stood at the north wall (Jeremiah 31:38; Zechariah 14:10). The Tower of the Hundred may be named for its height or for a company of a hundred men; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: they consecrated it: they set it apart for God
decisions.reason: The priests dedicated their section, the part beside the temple, to God. The whole wall was dedicated when it was finished (12:27-43).

decisions.choice: the high priest
decisions.reason: "The great priest" is the Hebrew title of the high priest (Leviticus 21:10; Haggai 1:1).

source.text: וְעַל־יָד֥וֹ בָנ֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יְרֵח֑וֹסוְעַל־יָד֣וֹ בָנָ֔ה זַכּ֖וּר בֶּן־אִמְרִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at his hand built [the] men of Jericho, and at his hand built Zaccur son of Imri.

en.L: And at his side the men of Jericho built, and at their side Zaccur son of Imri built.
en.B: Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri built.
en.R: The men from the town of Jericho built the next part of the wall. Zaccur son of Imri built the part next to theirs.

decisions.choice: at his hand: next to him, the next section along the wall
decisions.reason: This phrase, and "after him" from verse 16 on, link each group to the section next to the one before it. "His" in "at his hand" refers back to the last builder named, whether a man or a group, so the next part of the wall is meant.

decisions.choice: the men of Jericho: people from a town in the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Many builders came from towns outside Jerusalem (verses 5, 7, 13). Jericho's people had returned from exile (Ezra 2:34).

decisions.choice: next to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "at his hand" means; Literal keeps "at his side", close to the Hebrew picture.

source.text: וְאֵת֙ שַׁ֣עַר הַדָּגִ֔ים בָּנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י הַסְּנָאָ֑ה הֵ֣מָּה קֵר֔וּהוּ וַֽיַּעֲמִ֨ידוּ֙ דַּלְתֹתָ֔יו מַנְעוּלָ֖יו וּבְרִיחָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the gate of the fish built [the] sons of Hassenaah; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

en.L: And the Fish Gate the sons of Hassenaah built. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
en.B: The people of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
en.R: The people of Hassenaah rebuilt the Fish Gate. They put in its wooden beams and set up its doors with their bolts and bars.

decisions.choice: the Fish Gate: a gate in the north wall
decisions.reason: It was probably where fish brought from the coast were sold (13:16; Zephaniah 1:10; 2 Chronicles 33:14).

decisions.choice: the sons of Hassenaah: the people of Senaah, most likely a town
decisions.reason: The name, with the article, is the same as Senaah in Ezra 2:35, which lists 3,630 of its people. It is most likely a place, so the "sons" are its people.

decisions.choice: beams, doors, bolts and bars: the parts of a city gate
decisions.reason: A gate had wooden beams over the opening, heavy doors, and locks: bolts, and bars laid across the doors from inside (Deuteronomy 3:5; Judges 16:3).

decisions.choice: the people of Hassenaah
decisions.reason: The project's wording for "sons of" a place: "the people of".

source.text: וְעַל־יָדָ֣ם הֶחֱזִ֗יק מְרֵמ֤וֹת בֶּן־אוּרִיָּה֙ בֶּן־הַקּ֔וֹץסוְעַל־יָדָ֣ם הֶחֱזִ֔יק מְשֻׁלָּ֥ם בֶּן־בֶּרֶכְיָ֖ה בֶּן־מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵ֑לסוְעַל־יָדָ֣ם הֶֽחֱזִ֔יק צָד֖וֹק בֶּֽן־בַּעֲנָֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at their hand repaired Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz; and at their hand repaired Meshullam son of Berekiah son of Meshezabel; and at their hand repaired Zadok son of Baana.

en.L: And at their side Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired. And at their side Meshullam son of Berekiah son of Meshezabel repaired. And at their side Zadok son of Baana repaired.
en.B: Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to him Meshullam son of Berekiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs. Next to him Zadok son of Baana made repairs.
en.R: Meremoth son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz repaired the next part. Meshullam son of Berekiah and grandson of Meshezabel repaired the part after that, and Zadok son of Baana the next.

decisions.choice: repaired: made strong, restored
decisions.reason: The verb means to make strong. From here on it is the usual word for the work: some sections were rebuilt, others repaired where the old wall still stood.

decisions.choice: Meremoth and Meshullam: men named again in Ezra and Nehemiah
decisions.reason: Meremoth, of the priestly family of Hakkoz, received the temple silver and gold that Ezra brought (Ezra 8:33); he repaired a second section in verse 21. Meshullam repaired another section in verse 30, and his daughter married Tobiah's son (6:18).

decisions.choice: next to
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "at his hand" means the next section along the wall, so Balanced and Readable say "next to".

source.text: וְעַל־יָדָ֖ם הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ הַתְּקוֹעִ֑ים וְאַדִּֽירֵיהֶם֙ לֹא־הֵבִ֣יאוּ צַוָּרָ֔ם בַּעֲבֹדַ֖ת אֲדֹנֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at their hand repaired the Tekoites, and their nobles not brought their neck into [the] service of their lords.

en.L: And at their side the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles did not bring their neck to the service of their lords.
en.B: Next to them the men of Tekoa made repairs, but their nobles would not bow their necks to the work of their masters.
en.R: Next to them the men from Tekoa did repairs. But their leaders refused to work under the men in charge.

decisions.choice: the Tekoites: the people of Tekoa, a town south of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Tekoa was the home of the prophet Amos (Amos 1:1). Its people repaired a second section too (verse 27), even though their leaders held back.

decisions.choice: did not bring their neck into the service: refused to bend to the work
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that will not put its neck under the yoke (Jeremiah 27:11-12). The nobles thought the work beneath them, or refused to take part.

decisions.choice: their lords: those over them, most likely the men directing the work
decisions.reason: The word is plural, "lords" or "masters". It most likely means Nehemiah and the officials in charge of the work. It may also be read as "their Lord", God, since this plural form is sometimes used of God.

decisions.choice: nobles (Literal, Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2:16.

source.text: וְאֵת֩ שַׁ֨עַר הַיְשָׁנָ֜ה הֶחֱזִ֗יקוּ יֽוֹיָדָע֙ בֶּן־פָּסֵ֔חַ וּמְשֻׁלָּ֖ם בֶּן־בְּסֽוֹדְיָ֑ה הֵ֣מָּה קֵר֔וּהוּ וַֽיַּעֲמִ֨ידוּ֙ דַּלְתֹתָ֔יו וּמַנְעֻלָ֖יו וּבְרִיחָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the gate of the Jeshanah repaired Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah; they laid its beams and set up its doors and its bolts and its bars.

en.L: And the Jeshanah Gate Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired. They laid its beams and set up its doors and its bolts and its bars.
en.B: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Jeshanah Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
en.R: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Jeshanah Gate. They put in its beams and set up its doors with their bolts and bars.

decisions.choice: the Jeshanah Gate: a gate of the northwest, named either "the old" or for the town of Jeshanah
decisions.reason: The name means "the old". It may be "the Old Gate", an old gate of the city, or the gate on the road north to the town of Jeshanah (2 Chronicles 13:19), as a gate could be named for where its road led. The name comes again in 12:39.

source.text: וְעַל־יָדָ֨ם הֶחֱזִ֜יק מְלַטְיָ֣ה הַגִּבְעֹנִ֗י וְיָדוֹן֙ הַמֵּרֹ֣נֹתִ֔י אַנְשֵׁ֥י גִבְע֖וֹן וְהַמִּצְפָּ֑ה לְכִסֵּ֕א פַּחַ֖ת עֵ֥בֶר הַנָּהָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at their hand repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, [the] men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, for [the] seat of [the] governor of Beyond the River.

en.L: And at their side Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite repaired, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah, which belonged to the seat of the governor of Beyond the River.
en.B: Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite made repairs. They were men of Gibeon and Mizpah, which were under the authority of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
en.R: Next to them Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth did repairs with the men from Gibeon and Mizpah. These towns were under the governor of the province west of the Euphrates River.

decisions.choice: Gibeon and Mizpah: towns a few miles north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Gibeon (Joshua 9) and Mizpah (1 Samuel 7:5-6) lay in the land of Benjamin. After Jerusalem fell, Mizpah had been the seat of the governor Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jeremiah 40:6).

decisions.choice: for the seat of the governor of Beyond the River: the phrase is obscure
alternatives: as far as the residence of the governor of Beyond the River
decisions.reason: Word for word it says "to the seat (or throne) of the governor of Beyond the River". It may mean that these towns came under the provincial governor's own authority rather than Judah's, or that Mizpah held his residence for visits; or that these men repaired the wall as far as the governor's residence in Jerusalem. This record takes the first reading.

decisions.choice: next to; the province Beyond the River (Balanced), the province west of the Euphrates River (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "at his hand" means the next section along the wall, so Balanced and Readable say "next to". The province name follows 2:7.

source.text: עַל־יָד֣וֹ הֶחֱזִ֗יק עֻזִּיאֵ֤ל בֶּֽן־חַרְהֲיָה֙ צֽוֹרְפִ֔יםסוְעַל־יָד֣וֹ הֶחֱזִ֔יק חֲנַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן־הָרַקָּחִ֑ים וַיַּֽעַזְבוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַ֖ד הַחוֹמָ֥ה הָרְחָבָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: At his hand repaired Uzziel son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths; and at his hand repaired Hananiah, son of the perfumers; and they restored Jerusalem as far as the wall, the broad.

en.L: At his side Uzziel son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths, repaired, and at his side Hananiah, one of the perfumers, repaired. And they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
en.B: Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him Hananiah, one of the perfume makers, made repairs. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
en.R: Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah did repairs; he was a goldsmith. Next to him Hananiah did repairs; he made perfumes. They restored the city as far as the Broad Wall.

decisions.choice: goldsmiths, son of the perfumers: members of craft guilds
decisions.reason: "Son of the perfumers" means one of the perfumers, a member of the trade. Craftsmen worked on the wall beside priests and town leaders (also verses 31-32).

decisions.choice: they restored: the sense of the verb is uncertain
alternatives: they left (unbuilt) Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall
decisions.reason: The verb is usually "leave" or "abandon". Here it most likely means "restore" or "repair", a less common sense of the same letters. Read as "leave", the clause would mean that they left a part of Jerusalem unwalled as far as the Broad Wall.

decisions.choice: the Broad Wall: a thick stretch of wall on the west or northwest
decisions.reason: The Broad Wall is named again in 12:38. Remains of a very thick wall from the time of the kings have been found in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City, which may be this wall or part of the same line.

decisions.choice: next to
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "at his hand" means the next section along the wall, so Balanced and Readable say "next to".

source.text: וְעַל־יָדָ֤ם הֶחֱזִיק֙ רְפָיָ֣ה בֶן־ח֔וּר שַׂ֕ר חֲצִ֖י פֶּ֥לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at their hand repaired Rephaiah son of Hur, prince of half [the] district of Jerusalem.

en.L: And at their side Rephaiah son of Hur, prince of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired.
en.B: Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, official over half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
en.R: Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur did repairs. He was the leader of half the district of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: official of half the district: the head of an administrative area of Judah
decisions.reason: Judah under Persia was divided into districts, some of them in halves: Jerusalem (verses 9, 12), Beth-haccherem (verse 14), Mizpah (verses 15, 19), Beth-zur (verse 16) and Keilah (verses 17-18). Each had an official at its head, and several of them took a section of the wall.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for this title of rank.

source.text: וְעַל־יָדָ֧ם הֶחֱזִ֛יק יְדָיָ֥ה בֶן־חֲרוּמַ֖ף וְנֶ֣גֶד בֵּית֑וֹסוְעַל־יָד֣וֹ הֶחֱזִ֔יק חַטּ֖וּשׁ בֶּן־חֲשַׁבְנְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And at their hand repaired Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and opposite his house; and at his hand repaired Hattush son of Hashabneiah.

en.L: And at their side Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired, opposite his own house. And at his side Hattush son of Hashabneiah repaired.
en.B: Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
en.R: Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph did repairs across from his own house. Hattush son of Hashabneiah did the next part.

decisions.choice: opposite his house: men repaired the wall near their own homes
decisions.reason: Several builders repaired the stretch facing their own houses (verses 23, 28-30). Each had a reason to do it well, since the wall protected his own household.

decisions.choice: next to
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "at his hand" means the next section along the wall, so Balanced and Readable say "next to".

source.text: מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֗ית הֶחֱזִיק֙ מַלְכִּיָּ֣ה בֶן־חָרִ֔ם וְחַשּׁ֖וּב בֶּן־פַּחַ֣ת מוֹאָ֑ב וְאֵ֖ת מִגְדַּ֥ל הַתַּנּוּרִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: A second measure repaired Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab, and the tower of the ovens.

en.L: A second section Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired, and the Tower of the Ovens.
en.B: Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, and the Tower of the Ovens.
en.R: Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, including the Tower of the Ovens.

decisions.choice: a second measure: another measured section
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of builders who did more than one section (verses 19-21, 24, 27, 30). For these two men no first section is named; "second" may mean that the list does not give it, or simply "another".

decisions.choice: Harim, Pahath-moab and the Tower of the Ovens
decisions.reason: Harim and Pahath-moab ("governor of Moab") are family names among the returned exiles (Ezra 2:6, 32, 39). The Tower of the Ovens, on the west wall, may have stood near where bread was baked (Jeremiah 37:21) or near kilns.

decisions.choice: another section
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "another" for "second", since the first is not named; Literal keeps "second".

source.text: וְעַל־יָד֣וֹ הֶחֱזִ֗יק שַׁלּוּם֙ בֶּן־הַלּוֹחֵ֔שׁ שַׂ֕ר חֲצִ֖י פֶּ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם ה֖וּא וּבְנוֹתָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And at his hand repaired Shallum son of Hallohesh, prince of half [the] district of Jerusalem, he and his daughters.

en.L: And at his side Shallum son of Hallohesh, prince of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.
en.B: Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, official over the other half of the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, he and his daughters.
en.R: Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh did repairs. He was the leader of the other half of the district of Jerusalem. His daughters worked with him.

decisions.choice: he and his daughters: his daughters worked beside him
decisions.reason: Most likely his own daughters, who joined in the work; the text names no sons. "Daughters" can also mean the villages that belong to a town (Numbers 21:25; Nehemiah 11:25), so it may mean the villages of his district, but "he and" points to people.

decisions.choice: the other half
decisions.reason: Verse 9 named the official over one half of the district; Balanced and Readable say "the other half", which follows from the two verses.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

source.text: אֵת֩ שַׁ֨עַר הַגַּ֜יְא הֶחֱזִ֣יק חָנוּן֮ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י זָנוֹחַ֒ הֵ֣מָּה בָנ֔וּהוּ וַֽיַּעֲמִ֨ידוּ֙ דַּלְתֹתָ֔יו מַנְעֻלָ֖יו וּבְרִיחָ֑יו וְאֶ֤לֶף אַמָּה֙ בַּחוֹמָ֔ה עַ֖ד שַׁ֥עַר הָשֲׁפֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: The gate of the valley repaired Hanun and [the] inhabitants of Zanoah; they built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and a thousand cubits in the wall as far as [the] gate of the dung.

en.L: The Valley Gate Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired. They built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and repaired 1,000 cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
en.B: Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. They also repaired {{units:about 1,500 feet|1,000 cubits}} of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate.
en.R: Hanun and the people from Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it and set up its doors with their bolts and bars. They also repaired {{units:about 1,500 feet|1,000 cubits}} of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate.

decisions.choice: the Valley Gate and Zanoah
decisions.reason: The Valley Gate is where Nehemiah began his night inspection (2:13). Zanoah was a town in the low hills west of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:34; 11:30).

decisions.choice: a thousand cubits to the Dung Gate: a long stretch
decisions.reason: A cubit was about 18 inches, so this was about 1,500 feet of wall, the only section in the list whose length is given. The old wall here may have needed less repair, or it was the long south-western stretch down to the Dung Gate (2:13).

decisions.choice: 1,000 cubits (Literal); a units span with about 1,500 feet (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew unit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the cubit as the alternative.

source.text: וְאֵ֣ת׀שַׁ֣עַר הָאַשְׁפּ֗וֹת הֶחֱזִיק֙ מַלְכִּיָּ֣ה בֶן־רֵכָ֔ב שַׂ֖ר פֶּ֣לֶךְ בֵּית־הַכָּ֑רֶם ה֣וּא יִבְנֶ֔נּוּ וְיַעֲמִיד֙ דַּלְתֹתָ֔יו מַנְעֻלָ֖יו וּבְרִיחָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the gate of the dung repaired Malkijah son of Rechab, prince of [the] district of Beth-haccherem; he built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

en.L: And the Dung Gate Malkijah son of Rechab, prince of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired. He built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
en.B: Malkijah son of Rechab, official over the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate. He rebuilt it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
en.R: Malkijah son of Rechab, the leader of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate. He rebuilt it and set up its doors with their bolts and bars.

decisions.choice: the Dung Gate and Beth-haccherem
decisions.reason: The Dung Gate, at the south end of the city, led out to where refuse was taken (2:13). Beth-haccherem ("house of the vineyard") was a town of Judah near Jerusalem, a place for signal fires (Jeremiah 6:1).

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.literal_gloss: And the gate of the spring repaired Shallun son of Col-hozeh, prince of [the] district of Mizpah; he built it and roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars; and [the] wall of [the] pool of Shelah of [the] garden of the king, and as far as the steps going down from [the] city of David.

en.L: And the Fountain Gate Shallun son of Col-hozeh, prince of the district of Mizpah, repaired. He built it and roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps going down from the City of David.
en.B: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, official over the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it, roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
en.R: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, the leader of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it, put a roof over it, and set up its doors with their bolts and bars. He also repaired the wall by the Pool of Shelah near the king's garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.

decisions.choice: the Fountain Gate and the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden: the southeast corner of the city
decisions.reason: The Fountain Gate is named in 2:14. The Pool of Shelah is most likely the pool of Siloam (Shiloah in Isaiah 8:6; John 9:7), fed by a channel from the Gihon spring; the king's garden lay near it in the valley (2 Kings 25:4).

decisions.choice: the steps going down from the City of David
decisions.reason: The City of David was the old city on the southeastern ridge, which David took (2 Samuel 5:7-9). Steps led down its steep east side; they are named again in 12:37.

decisions.choice: roofed it: covered the gateway
decisions.reason: The verb means to cover or shade. A gateway was a covered passage through the wall, with rooms or a tower above.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Nehemiah son of Azbuk, prince of half [the] district of Beth-zur, as far as opposite [the] graves of David and as far as the pool, the made [one], and as far as [the] house of the mighty men.

en.L: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, prince of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired as far as opposite the graves of David, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men.
en.B: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, official over half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs as far as a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the man-made pool and the house of the warriors.
en.R: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, the leader of half the district of Beth-zur, did repairs. He worked as far as the place across from the tombs of King David, as far as the pool that had been dug and the soldiers' barracks.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah son of Azbuk: another man of the same name
decisions.reason: He is not the governor who writes the book, who is "son of Hacaliah" (1:1). Beth-zur was a town on the road south toward Hebron.

decisions.choice: the graves of David: the royal tombs in the City of David
decisions.reason: David and the kings after him were buried in the City of David (1 Kings 2:10; 2 Chronicles 32:33). From here on the list goes north along the east side of the city.

decisions.choice: the made pool and the house of the mighty men: places along the east wall
decisions.reason: "The pool that was made" is a man-made reservoir, perhaps one made by King Hezekiah (2 Kings 20:20; Isaiah 22:11). "The house of the mighty men" was most likely a barracks for soldiers, perhaps once for David's warriors (2 Samuel 23:8). Neither place has been identified for certain.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

source.text: אַחֲרָ֛יו הֶחֱזִ֥יקוּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם רְח֣וּם בֶּן־בָּנִ֑י עַל־יָד֣וֹ הֶחֱזִ֗יק חֲשַׁבְיָ֛ה שַׂר־חֲצִי־פֶ֥לֶךְ קְעִילָ֖ה לְפִלְכּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired the Levites: Rehum son of Bani; at his hand repaired Hashabiah, prince of half [the] district of Keilah, for his district.

en.L: After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani. At his side Hashabiah, prince of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his district.
en.B: After him the Levites made repairs, under Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, official over half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
en.R: After him the Levites did repairs, led by Rehum son of Bani. Next to them Hashabiah, the leader of half the district of Keilah, did repairs for the people of his district.

decisions.choice: the Levites: the tribe that served at the temple
decisions.reason: The Levites assisted the priests in the temple's service (Numbers 3:5-9; Ezra 3:8-9). Here they work as one group, like the priests in verse 1.

decisions.choice: for his district: on behalf of the people of his half-district
decisions.reason: Hashabiah worked for the district he governed; the other half of Keilah's district built under its own leader (verse 18). Keilah was a town in the low hills southwest of Jerusalem (1 Samuel 23:1).

decisions.choice: under Rehum (Balanced); led by Rehum (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Rehum right after "the Levites", most likely as their leader for this section. Balanced and Readable make that link.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired their brothers: Bavvai son of Henadad, prince of half [the] district of Keilah.

en.L: After him their brothers repaired: Bavvai son of Henadad, prince of half the district of Keilah.
en.B: After him their fellow Levites made repairs, under Bavvai son of Henadad, official over the other half of the district of Keilah.
en.R: After him more Levites did repairs. They were led by Bavvai son of Henadad, the leader of the other half of the district of Keilah.

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow Levites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means members of the same group, the Levites of verse 17.

decisions.choice: Bavvai son of Henadad: perhaps the same man as Binnui son of Henadad
decisions.reason: Verse 24 names "Binnui son of Henadad", and Binnui is a Levite name (10:10; 12:8). The two names differ by one letter in Hebrew, so they may be the same man with the name copied differently, or two members of one family. The text as it stands is translated.

decisions.choice: fellow Levites; the other half
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "their brothers" are and, as in verse 12, that this is the other half of the district.

records.literal_gloss: And repaired at his hand Ezer son of Jeshua, prince of Mizpah, a second measure, from opposite [the] going up of the armory, the angle.

en.L: And at his side Ezer son of Jeshua, prince of Mizpah, repaired a second section, from opposite the ascent to the armory, at the Angle.
en.B: Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, official of Mizpah, repaired another section, from a point opposite the way up to the armory, at the Angle.
en.R: Next to them Ezer son of Jeshua, the leader of Mizpah, repaired another section. It began across from the road up to the armory, where the wall turns a corner.

decisions.choice: the ascent to the armory, the Angle: a corner of the eastern wall
decisions.reason: The armory was a store of weapons. "The Angle" is a place where the wall turned or jutted out (2 Chronicles 26:9; Nehemiah 3:20, 24-25). These were landmarks on the east side, below the royal buildings.

decisions.choice: a second measure: another section
decisions.reason: As in verse 11: "second" means another section. Ezer is not named earlier in the list.

decisions.choice: next to; another section
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "at his hand" means the next section along the wall, so Balanced and Readable say "next to". "Second" is "another" as in verse 11.

decisions.choice: prince (Literal); official (Balanced); leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.literal_gloss: After him burned [with zeal and] repaired Baruch son of Zaccai a second measure, from the angle as far as [the] door of [the] house of Eliashib the priest, the great.

en.L: After him Baruch son of Zaccai eagerly repaired a second section, from the Angle as far as the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
en.B: After him Baruch son of Zaccai eagerly repaired another section, from the Angle as far as the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
en.R: After him Baruch son of Zaccai worked hard to repair another section. It ran from the corner as far as the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

decisions.choice: burned: he worked with zeal
decisions.reason: The verb means "burn" or "be hot", here most likely of zeal: he repaired eagerly. A small change in its letters would give "toward the hill", but the text as it stands is translated.

decisions.choice: Zaccai: the name as read; the written text has Zabbai
decisions.reason: The consonants of the text spell the name Zabbai (as in Ezra 10:28); the Masoretic reading tradition reads Zaccai (as in Ezra 2:9). The source data follows the reading, and so does this record.

decisions.choice: the house of Eliashib the high priest: beside the temple, on the east
decisions.reason: The high priest's house stood near the temple. The builders of verses 20-21 measure their sections by its door and its end.

decisions.choice: another section
decisions.reason: "Second" is "another" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz a second measure, from [the] door of [the] house of Eliashib and as far as [the] end of [the] house of Eliashib.

en.L: After him Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired a second section, from the door of the house of Eliashib as far as the end of the house of Eliashib.
en.B: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of his house.
en.R: After him Meremoth son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz repaired another section. It ran from the door of Eliashib's house to the far end of it.

decisions.choice: Meremoth's second section
decisions.reason: Meremoth had already repaired a section on the north wall (verse 4). His second runs only the length of the high priest's house, perhaps because it was a hard stretch.

decisions.choice: another section
decisions.reason: "Second" is "another" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: And after him repaired the priests, [the] men of the plain.

en.L: And after him the priests, the men of the surrounding region, repaired.
en.B: After him the priests from the surrounding region made repairs.
en.R: After him the priests who lived in the area around Jerusalem did repairs.

decisions.choice: the plain: the region around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means a round area or district. It is most often used of the Jordan valley (Genesis 13:10), but in 12:28 it is the country around Jerusalem, where singers had their villages. Either may be meant here; the nearer region is more likely.

decisions.choice: the area around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the region as the sense decided above.

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Benjamin and Hasshub opposite their house; after him repaired Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah beside his house.

en.L: After him Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah repaired beside his own house.
en.B: After them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house, and after them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his own house.
en.R: After them Benjamin and Hasshub did repairs across from their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah and grandson of Ananiah did repairs beside his own house.

decisions.choice: opposite their house, beside his house: men repaired by their homes
decisions.reason: As in verse 10: along this eastern stretch many builders repaired the wall in front of their own houses (verses 28-30).

decisions.choice: after them
decisions.reason: "After him" refers to the last builder named; where that was two men, Balanced and Readable say "them".

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Binnui son of Henadad a second measure, from [the] house of Azariah as far as the angle and as far as the corner.

en.L: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired a second section, from the house of Azariah as far as the Angle and as far as the corner.
en.B: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the Angle and to the corner.
en.R: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section. It ran from Azariah's house to the place where the wall turns, at the corner.

decisions.choice: Binnui son of Henadad: a Levite family
decisions.reason: Henadad was a family of Levites (Ezra 3:9; Nehemiah 10:10). Binnui may be the Bavvai of verse 18.

decisions.choice: the Angle and the corner: where the wall bent
decisions.reason: The first word is a turn or jutting part of the wall (verse 19); the second is a corner. They are landmarks on the east side, perhaps one bend.

decisions.choice: another section
decisions.reason: "Second" is "another" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: Palal son of Uzai, from opposite the angle and the tower projecting from [the] house of the king, the upper, which [is] at [the] courtyard of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh.

en.L: Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the Angle and the tower that projects from the upper house of the king, at the courtyard of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh repaired.
en.B: Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the Angle and the tower that projects from the upper palace of the king, at the courtyard of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh made repairs
en.R: Palal son of Uzai did repairs across from the corner and the tower that sticks out from the king's upper palace, near the courtyard of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh did repairs

decisions.choice: Palal ... Pedaiah: the verb "repaired" is understood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the names and places; the verb of the verses before is carried over. Pedaiah's clause runs on into verse 26, which names the place he reached.

decisions.choice: the tower projecting from the king's upper house, at the courtyard of the guard: the old royal palace
decisions.reason: The kings' palace stood south of the temple, above the City of David. Its "courtyard of the guard" is where Jeremiah was held (Jeremiah 32:2; 37:21). The "upper" house may mean the higher part of the palace or a separate upper palace.

decisions.choice: made repairs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the understood verb. Their last clause runs into verse 26, so they end without a full stop.

source.text: וְהַ֨נְּתִינִ֔ים הָי֥וּ יֹשְׁבִ֖ים בָּעֹ֑פֶל עַ֠ד נֶ֜גֶד שַׁ֤עַר הַמַּ֨יִם֙ לַמִּזְרָ֔ח וְהַמִּגְדָּ֖ל הַיּוֹצֵֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the Nethinim were dwelling on the Ophel, as far as opposite [the] gate of the water toward the east and the tower, the projecting.

en.L: And the Nethinim were living on the Ophel, as far as opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
en.B: (the temple servants were living on the Ophel) as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
en.R: (the temple servants lived on the hill called Ophel) as far as the place across from the Water Gate on the east side and the tower that sticks out.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim: the temple servants
decisions.reason: The name means "those given": people given to serve at the temple in the work of the Levites (Ezra 2:43; 8:20). They lived near the temple (11:21).

decisions.choice: the Ophel and the Water Gate
decisions.reason: The Ophel ("swelling" or "mound") is the rise between the City of David and the temple (2 Chronicles 27:3). The Water Gate on the east led down toward the Gihon spring; the people later gathered at a square before it to hear the law (8:1, 3).

decisions.choice: the temple servants were living on the Ophel: a note, or the subject of the repair
decisions.reason: The verse has no "repaired". It may be a note on where the temple servants lived, with "as far as" completing Pedaiah's section in verse 25, or it may say that the temple servants repaired up to the Water Gate. Balanced and Readable take the first reading and set the clause in parentheses.

decisions.choice: the temple servants
decisions.reason: The project's wording for the Nethinim: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, Balanced and Readable say what they were.

source.text: אַחֲרָ֛יו הֶחֱזִ֥יקוּ הַתְּקֹעִ֖ים מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֑ית מִנֶּ֜גֶד הַמִּגְדָּ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ הַיּוֹצֵ֔א וְעַ֖ד חוֹמַ֥ת הָעֹֽפֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired the Tekoites a second measure, from opposite the tower, the great, the projecting, and as far as [the] wall of the Ophel.

en.L: After him the Tekoites repaired a second section, from opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.
en.B: After them the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from a point opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.
en.R: After them the men from Tekoa repaired another section. It ran from the place across from the great tower that sticks out, as far as the wall of the Ophel.

decisions.choice: the Tekoites' second section
decisions.reason: The men of Tekoa did a second section although their nobles would not work (verse 5).

decisions.choice: another section; after them
decisions.reason: "Second" is "another" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 11. "Him" refers to the last builder named, here a group, so Balanced and Readable say "them".

source.text: מֵעַ֣ל׀שַׁ֣עַר הַסּוּסִ֗ים הֶחֱזִ֨יקוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ לְנֶ֥גֶד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Above [the] gate of the horses repaired the priests, each opposite his house.

en.L: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.
en.B: Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his own house.
en.R: North of the Horse Gate the priests did repairs, each one across from his own house.

decisions.choice: the Horse Gate: a gate on the east, near the temple and palace
decisions.reason: The Horse Gate stood at the east side of the city by the royal buildings (2 Kings 11:16; Jeremiah 31:40). The priests lived near the temple, so they repaired the wall by their homes.

decisions.choice: above: up from, north of the gate
decisions.reason: "Above" here most likely means upward along the wall from the gate, which on this east side is toward the north.

decisions.choice: North of
decisions.reason: Readable says the direction that "above" most likely means here; it follows the reading of the decision above.

source.text: אַחֲרָ֧יו הֶחֱזִ֛יק צָד֥וֹק בֶּן־אִמֵּ֖ר נֶ֣גֶד בֵּית֑וֹסוְאַחֲרָ֤יו הֶחֱזִיק֙ שְׁמַֽעְיָ֣ה בֶן־שְׁכַנְיָ֔ה שֹׁמֵ֖ר שַׁ֥עַר הַמִּזְרָֽח׃ס

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Zadok son of Immer opposite his house; and after him repaired Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of [the] gate of the east.

en.L: After him Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
en.B: After them Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his own house, and after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
en.R: After them Zadok son of Immer did repairs across from his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah did repairs. He was the guard of the East Gate.

decisions.choice: keeper of the East Gate: a gatekeeper, probably of the temple's east gate
decisions.reason: Gatekeepers were Levites who guarded the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 26:12-18). The East Gate here may be the temple's east gate (compare Ezekiel 40:6) or a gate of the city.

decisions.choice: after them
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, "him" refers back to the priests of verse 28.

source.text: אַחֲרָ֨יו הֶחֱזִ֜יק חֲנַנְיָ֣ה בֶן־שֶׁלֶמְיָ֗ה וְחָנ֧וּן בֶּן־צָלָ֛ף הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֑יסאַחֲרָ֣יו הֶחֱזִ֗יק מְשֻׁלָּם֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד נִשְׁכָּתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph a second measure. After him repaired Meshullam son of Berekiah opposite his room.

en.L: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berekiah repaired opposite his room.
en.B: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After them Meshullam son of Berekiah made repairs opposite his living quarters.
en.R: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After them Meshullam son of Berekiah did repairs across from the rooms where he lived.

decisions.choice: his room: his chamber, perhaps a room in the temple buildings
decisions.reason: The word is used of the rooms around the temple courts (10:38-40; 13:4-5). Meshullam, who repaired another section in verse 4, may have lived in such rooms or in quarters of his own.

decisions.choice: another section; after them
decisions.reason: "Second" is "another" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 11. The second "after him" follows two builders, so Balanced and Readable say "them".

source.text: אַחֲרָ֣יו הֶחֱזִ֗יק מַלְכִּיָּה֙ בֶּן־הַצֹּ֣רְפִ֔י עַד־בֵּ֥ית הַנְּתִינִ֖ים וְהָרֹכְלִ֑ים נֶ֚גֶד שַׁ֣עַר הַמִּפְקָ֔ד וְעַ֖ד עֲלִיַּ֥ת הַפִּנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: After him repaired Malkijah, son of the goldsmith, as far as [the] house of the Nethinim and the merchants, opposite [the] gate of the muster, and as far as [the] upper room of the corner.

en.L: After him Malkijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the Nethinim and of the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room of the corner.
en.B: After him Malkijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper room at the corner.
en.R: After him Malkijah, a goldsmith, did repairs as far as the building used by the temple servants and the traders. It was across from the Inspection Gate. He worked as far as the room on top of the corner of the wall.

decisions.choice: the Muster Gate: a gate on the northeast, of uncertain purpose
decisions.reason: The name means "gate of the appointed place", "of mustering" or "of inspection". It may be where troops were counted or where goods were checked; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the house of the temple servants and the merchants
decisions.reason: A building near the temple used by the temple servants and by traders, perhaps those who sold animals and goods for the offerings.

decisions.choice: the upper room of the corner: a room on the wall at its northeast corner
decisions.reason: This is the last landmark before the list returns to the Sheep Gate where it began (verse 32; verse 1).

decisions.choice: the Inspection Gate (Balanced, Readable); the Muster Gate (Literal)
decisions.reason: Both are English for the gate's name; Literal keeps the more literal sense "muster", Balanced and Readable a plainer word.

source.text: וּבֵ֨ין עֲלִיַּ֤ת הַפִּנָּה֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הַצֹּ֔אן הֶחֱזִ֥יקוּ הַצֹּרְפִ֖ים וְהָרֹכְלִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And between [the] upper room of the corner and [the] gate of the sheep repaired the goldsmiths and the merchants.

en.L: And between the upper room of the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants repaired.
en.B: Between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
en.R: The goldsmiths and the traders repaired the wall between the room on top of the corner and the Sheep Gate.

decisions.choice: the Sheep Gate: the circuit is complete
decisions.reason: The list ends where it began (verse 1). Every stretch of the wall has been assigned, from priests and officials to craftsmen and traders.

decisions.choice: the merchants: traders
decisions.reason: The word means traders who travel and sell, here people of the trade living near the temple (verse 31).

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר שָׁמַ֣ע סַנְבַלַּ֗ט כִּֽי־אֲנַ֤חְנוּ בוֹנִים֙ אֶת־הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַיִּ֣חַר ל֔וֹ וַיִּכְעַ֖ס הַרְבֵּ֑ה וַיַּלְעֵ֖ג עַל־הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Sanballat that we [were] building the wall, and it burned to him, and he was angry greatly, and he mocked about the Jews.

en.L: And it came about, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, that he was furious and very angry, and he mocked the Jews.
en.B: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and very angry, and he mocked the Jews.
en.R: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became furious. He was very angry, and he made fun of the Jews.

decisions.choice: verse numbering: Hebrew 3:33-38 is 4:1-6 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text, followed here, continues chapter 3 for six more verses, which many Bibles number 4:1-6. So Hebrew 4:1-17 is 4:7-23 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ. This translation cites Nehemiah by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: it burned to him: he was furious
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as burning (Genesis 4:5; Jonah 4:1). With "he was very angry" it shows how strongly Sanballat reacted to the wall going up.

decisions.choice: Sanballat mocked the Jews
decisions.reason: Sanballat, governor of Samaria (2:10, 19), had opposed the plan from the start. Ridicule was his first weapon; threats of attack follow (4:2).

decisions.choice: was furious (Literal, Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the order of the Hebrew clauses but says "was furious" for "it burned to him", since a word-for-word rendering is not English; the gloss keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לִפְנֵ֣י אֶחָ֗יו וְחֵיל֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֛ה הַיְּהוּדִ֥ים הָאֲמֵלָלִ֖ים עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲיַעַזְב֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם הֲיִזְבָּ֨חוּ֙ הַיְכַלּ֣וּ בַיּ֔וֹם הַיְחַיּ֧וּ אֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֛ים מֵעֲרֵמ֥וֹת הֶעָפָ֖ר וְהֵ֥מָּה שְׂרוּפֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said before his brothers and [the] army of Samaria, and he said, what [are] the Jews, the feeble, doing? Will they restore [it] for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones from [the] heaps of the rubble, and they [are] burned?

en.L: And he spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria and said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
en.B: He spoke in front of his associates and the army of Samaria and said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
en.R: In front of his friends and the soldiers of Samaria he said, "What do these weak Jews think they are doing? Do they think they can rebuild the wall on their own? Will they offer sacrifices and expect it to be done? Will they finish it in one day? These stones are piles of burned rubble. Can they make them new again?"

decisions.choice: his brothers and the army of Samaria: his associates and the troops of his province
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means his colleagues or allies. "The army of Samaria" may be the soldiers of the province or its leading men of wealth; the word can mean both. The speech is made before a force that could act.

decisions.choice: will they restore it for themselves: the verb is uncertain
alternatives: will they leave it to themselves?
decisions.reason: This is the same uncertain verb as in verse 8, most likely "restore". It may also be read as "will they be left to themselves", that is, will anyone let them do this.

decisions.choice: will they sacrifice? will they finish in a day?: mocking their faith and their haste
decisions.reason: The questions scorn the builders: will they pray and offer sacrifices and expect the wall to stand at once? Sacrifices were also offered at the dedication of a finished work (12:43).

decisions.choice: revive the stones from the heaps of rubble, though burned: the stones are ruined
decisions.reason: Limestone burned in a fire cracks and crumbles. To "revive" such stones, to make them live again, is something Sanballat thinks impossible.

decisions.choice: his associates (Balanced); his friends (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is not family here; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: Will they offer sacrifices and expect it to be done? ... These stones are piles of burned rubble. Can they make them new again?
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the mockery the short questions imply and splits the last question so a new reader can follow it.

source.text: וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה הָעַמֹּנִ֖י אֶצְל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֚ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֣ם בּוֹנִ֔ים אִם־יַעֲלֶ֣ה שׁוּעָ֔ל וּפָרַ֖ץ חוֹמַ֥ת אַבְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Tobiah the Ammonite [was] beside him, and he said, even what they [are] building, if goes up a fox, then it will break down their wall of stones.

en.L: And Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building, if a fox goes up on it, it will break down their stone wall!"
en.B: Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building, if a fox climbed up on it, it would break down their stone wall!"
en.R: Tobiah the Ammonite was standing beside him. He said, "Look at what they are building! If even a fox climbed up on that stone wall, it would fall down!"

decisions.choice: a fox: a small, light animal
decisions.reason: The word can mean a fox or a jackal (Judges 15:4; Lamentations 5:18). The point is that the wall is so weak that even a small animal's weight would bring it down.

decisions.choice: Tobiah the Ammonite: Sanballat's ally
decisions.reason: Tobiah (2:10, 19) joins Sanballat's mockery. Through his marriage ties to leading families in Jerusalem he could also stir trouble from inside (6:17-19).

decisions.choice: If even a fox climbed up on that stone wall, it would fall down
decisions.reason: Readable makes the wall the subject of the last clause, which says the same thing more simply: the fox's weight would bring it down.

source.text: שְׁמַ֤ע אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־הָיִ֣ינוּ בוּזָ֔ה וְהָשֵׁ֥ב חֶרְפָּתָ֖ם אֶל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם וּתְנֵ֥ם לְבִזָּ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שִׁבְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, our God, for we have become contempt; and return their taunt on their head, and give them to plunder in a land of captivity.

en.L: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt. Return their taunt on their own head, and give them up as plunder in a land of captivity.
en.B: Hear, our God, for we are despised! Turn their insults back on their own heads, and let them be plundered in a land where they are captives.
en.R: Listen, our God! They are treating us with scorn. Make their insults fall back on them. Let them be taken away as captives to a foreign land, and let others rob them.

decisions.choice: hear, our God: Nehemiah breaks off the account to pray
decisions.reason: As often in his memoir, Nehemiah turns from the story to a short prayer (5:19; 6:9, 14; 13:14). He does not answer the mockers; he brings it to God.

decisions.choice: return their taunt on their head, give them to plunder in captivity: a prayer for justice
decisions.reason: Nehemiah asks God to let the mockers suffer what they mocked, the plunder and exile that Judah had suffered (1:8; compare Psalm 79:12; Psalm 123:3-4). Such prayers hand vengeance to God rather than take it (Deuteronomy 32:35).

decisions.choice: on their head: on themselves
decisions.reason: To return something on someone's head is to make it fall back on them (Joel 4:4, 7; Psalm 7:17).

source.text: וְאַל־תְּכַס֙ עַל־עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֖ם מִלְּפָנֶ֣יךָ אַל־תִּמָּחֶ֑ה כִּ֥י הִכְעִ֖יסוּ לְנֶ֥גֶד הַבּוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not cover over their iniquity, and their sin from before you let it not be wiped out, for they have provoked to anger before the builders.

en.L: And do not cover over their iniquity, and let not their sin be wiped out from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for they have provoked [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] to anger before the builders.
en.B: Do not cover their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight, for they have provoked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to anger in front of the builders.
en.R: Do not forgive their guilt or erase their sin from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight. They have insulted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} angry in front of the people building the wall.

decisions.choice: do not cover their iniquity, let not their sin be wiped out: the words of Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Jeremiah prayed in almost the same words against those plotting against him (Jeremiah 18:23). To cover sin or wipe it out is to forgive it (Psalm 32:1; 51:3, 11).

decisions.choice: they have provoked to anger before the builders: they have provoked God, in front of the builders
alternatives: they have insulted the builders to their faces
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Most likely they have provoked God by mocking his people's work in their presence. It may also mean that they have provoked the builders, insulting them to their faces.

decisions.choice: provoked you (in brackets at Literal)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb has no object; all levels supply "you" (God), following the reading chosen above, and Literal marks it as supplied.

decisions.choice: forgive; erase
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what "cover" and "wipe out" mean for sin.

source.text: וַנִּבְנֶה֙ אֶת־הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַתִּקָּשֵׁ֥ר כָּל־הַחוֹמָ֖ה עַד־חֶצְיָ֑הּ וַיְהִ֧י לֵ֦ב לָעָ֖ם לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And we built the wall, and was joined together all the wall as far as its half, and was a heart to the people to work.

en.L: So we built the wall, and all the wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.
en.B: So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
en.R: So we kept building, and the whole wall was joined together up to half its full height. The people were eager to work.

decisions.choice: joined together as far as its half: the whole circuit closed, to half its height
decisions.reason: The gaps were closed all the way around, and the wall stood at half its intended height. "Half" refers to height, since the whole length was joined.

decisions.choice: there was a heart to the people to work: the people were set on working
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of will and purpose. The people were willing and determined, in spite of the mockery (verses 33-35).

decisions.choice: had a mind to work
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English idiom for will and purpose; Literal keeps "heart" and Readable says "eager".
